characters.continuity: New Super Mario Bros. (DS), with later appearances (New Super Mario Bros. 2, Mario & Luigi: Paper Jam)
characters.summary: Dry Bowser is the skeletal form Bowser takes after falling into lava in New Super Mario Bros. He throws his own bones, breathes fire (blue in later games) and is fireproof, but Mario beat him by dropping him into a pit.

techniques: Throws his own bones
Breathes small flames in New Super Mario Bros.; blue fire in later games
High jumps and a drop from the ceiling at the start of his fight
Mario & Luigi: Paper Jam: throws his head to spew blue flames, inhales foes, summons Thwomps and Koopalings

mechanisms: Fireproof like Dry Bones: Fire Mario's fireballs have no effect
His body falls apart when he lands after being thrown into a pit, and he reassembles for the World 8 fight

weaknesses: A skull switch destroys the bridge he stands on and drops him into a deep pit
A Mega Mushroom jump makes him crumble
Three shell-dash hits defeat him, as with living Bowser
characters.formDifferences: Bowser's skeleton after he fell into lava in World 1-Castle. He trades flesh for a fireproof skeletal body that throws bones. Bowser Jr. later tosses the bones into a cauldron and Bowser returns, larger and breathing blue fire.

sources.supports: Origin in New Super Mario Bros. World 1-Castle, attacks (bones, flames, jumps; Paper Jam moves), fireproofing, falling apart and reassembling, defeat by skull switch, Mega Mushroom or shell dashes, and reversion via Bowser Jr.'s cauldron

feats.claim: Fell into lava after his defeat in World 1-Castle and came back as the skeletal Dry Bowser

notableResults.note: Mario hit the skull switch, which destroyed the bridge and sent Dry Bowser into a deep pit

conditional.dependsOn: Bowser falling into lava; it ends when Bowser Jr. tosses the bones into a cauldron and Bowser revives

campaignTags.claim: Breathes flames, blue fire in later games

unknowns: Whether the skeleton can reassemble indefinitely is not stated; the page shows one reassembly between World 1 and World 8.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the cited Wikipedia page (not opened this run) with the Super Mario Wiki Dry Bowser page. Restored bone throwing and fire breath; fireproofing and falling apart/reassembling are now sourced. Removed "ground pound shockwaves", "immune to standard blunt force" and a collapse-on-impact limitation (not on the page). Tag `fire` narrowed to `fire-control`. Removed `magic` domain (no magic described).

characters.continuity: Bowser's Fury (Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury, 2021)
characters.summary: Fury Bowser is a gigantic kaiju form of Bowser created by splotchy black goop. He sleeps in the Fury Sun at the middle of Lake Lapcat and rampages at intervals, raining fire over the lake, until Giga Cat Mario defeats him.

techniques: Fury blasts: large beams of fire aimed at Mario; the only attack that destroys Fury Blocks
Fireballs that fall across the whole lake and leave circles of lava
Digs into the ground to summon large falling spikes
A shockwave of fire when he jumps at Mario
Later fights: a ring of huge fireballs and gigantic Kick Bombs

mechanisms: Gigantic size; his belly is exposed to Ground Pounds only when his shell is flipped
Claw swipes and lighthouse light deal only small damage outside that window

weaknesses: Flipping him exposes his belly to Ground Pounds; three Ground Pounds empty his health bar in the first battle
Lighthouse light damages him slightly
limitations: Sleeps in the Fury Sun between rampages, waking roughly every six minutes
A rampage ends after a while, or when the player collects a Cat Shine
characters.formDifferences: Bowser turned into a gigantic black-skinned kaiju by splotchy goop. He gains fire beams, lake-wide fireball rain and summoned spikes, but only Giga Cat Mario can fight him to a defeat.

sources.supports: Transformation by splotchy goop, kaiju size, fury blasts, fireballs, spikes, shockwave, sleep/wake cycle in the Fury Sun on Lake Lapcat, Giga Bell/Giga Cat Mario battles, Ground Pound weakness, lighthouse damage, Bowser Jr. in multiplayer

feats.claim: During rampages, fireballs fall across the whole of Lake Lapcat and leave circles of lava

notableResults.opponent: Mario (as Giga Cat Mario), with Bowser Jr.
notableResults.note: Mario collects Giga Bells to become Giga Cat Mario for five boss battles; depleting Fury Bowser's health is the only way to defeat him. Bowser Jr. can also attack him in multiplayer for less damage

conditional.dependsOn: Exposure to splotchy goop (the page implies Bowser Jr. painted him black as a prank)

campaignTags.claim: Described as a gigantic kaiju whose body dwarfs his head; fought only by Giga Cat Mario
Fury blasts of fire, lake-wide fireball rain and fire shockwaves

unknowns: The page gives no height figure; giant-sized rests on the kaiju description, which is far beyond 8 ft. Owner may want a numeric figure.
Whether he can swim is not stated; after his final defeat he hits the water and sinks back into the Fury Sun.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the cited Wikipedia page (not opened this run) with the Super Mario Wiki Fury Bowser page. Restored fire blasts and spike summons; removed "tidal wave leaps", "impenetrable shell" and swimming (not on the page). The Giga Bell weakness is reworded: the bells make Giga Cat Mario, who beats him. Tag `fire` narrowed to `fire-control`.

characters.continuity: Super Smash Bros. series (Melee hidden boss; Bowser's Final Smash in Brawl and SSB4; boss and Giga Bowser Punch in Ultimate)
characters.summary: Giga Bowser is a monstrous form almost twice Bowser's size. He has passive super armor and barely flinches, but in Smash he appears only as a boss or as a short Final Smash.

techniques: Fire Breath: a large stream of flames
Flying Slam (20%)
Bowser Bomb
Whirling Fortress
Giga Bowser Punch Final Smash in Ultimate (40%)

mechanisms: Passive super armor; takes minimal hitstun
Knockback threshold (20 KB subtractive in Melee; 95 KB non-subtractive in Ultimate)
Cannot be grabbed, inhaled or egg-laid

weaknesses: In Melee he can only be beaten by knocking him offstage
Misusing Flying Slam or Bowser Bomb can carry him off the stage for a KO
mobility: Walking and jumping as Bowser does
limitations: As a Final Smash in Brawl and SSB4 the transformation lasts only ten seconds
characters.formDifferences: A larger, horned, demonic Bowser, almost twice his size, with stronger offense and defense, passive super armor and grab immunity.

sources.supports: Melee Adventure Mode boss, Brawl/SSB4 ten-second Final Smash, Ultimate Giga Bowser Punch (40%), size about twice Bowser, super armor and knockback threshold, grab immunity, attacks and how he is defeated

conditional.dependsOn: Bowser's Final Smash (ten seconds in Brawl/SSB4) or a boss encounter

campaignTags.claim: Fire Breath: breathes a large stream of flames

unknowns: No height in feet: the page says only that he is almost twice as large as Bowser, so `giant-sized` is not granted under the ~8 ft ruling (consistent with base Bowser). Owner may rule on this.
The page notes his weight does not scale with size and in tests he is lighter than Bowser.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the cited Super Smash Bros. Melee Wikipedia page (not opened) with the SmashWiki Giga Bowser page. Removed the unsupported feat "fought off multiple Smash fighters" and the unnamed-opponent "roster" result. Tags: `giant-sized` removed, `fire` narrowed to `fire-control`.

characters.continuity: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
characters.summary: Calamity Ganon is the primal evil of Hyrule in its BotW form: Malice fused with Guardian parts. He turned the Guardian army against Hyrule a hundred years earlier, and in battle he combines all four Blight Ganons' elemental attacks.

techniques: Ice blocks like Waterblight Ganon
Fields of thunder spikes
Tornado gusts
A slow laser and a large laser beam
A fireball that ignites the battlefield
Swings a flaming sword and smaller blue swords
Throws a spear (second phase)

mechanisms: An impenetrable orange shield in the second phase that blocks arrows, melee weapons and elemental rods

weaknesses: Perfect Dodges trigger Flurry Rushes, and a Perfect Guard stuns him after a laser
A Perfect Guard, Daruk's Protection, a Flurry Rush or Urbosa's Fury drops his shield
Ancient and Guardian equipment deal extra damage, since he counts as a Guardian-type enemy
Loses 1/8 of his health for each Divine Beast freed
mobility: Centipede-like body; crashes to the ground in the second phase
limitations: Sealed and tethered to Hyrule Castle by Zelda for a hundred years
Link wakes him early, so he fights in an incomplete form

sources.supports: Nature (primal evil; Malice, Ganondorf and Guardian parts), corrupting the Guardian army, Blights seizing the Divine Beasts, Zelda's sealing, premature awakening by Link, and the 1/8 health loss per freed Divine Beast
Boss fight: ice blocks, thunder spikes, tornadoes, lasers, fireball, flaming sword, spear, orange shield, and how Link beats him (Perfect Dodge/Guard, Champion abilities, Ancient gear)

feats.claim: Used Malice to corrupt the entire Guardian army and turn it on the Hyrulians; his Blight Ganons took control of the four Divine Beasts after their pilots were slain
feats.citation: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild (the Great Calamity)

notableResults.citation: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Hyrule Castle
notableResults.note: Link fights him in an incomplete form after waking him early; the boss guide describes beating him with Perfect Dodges, Perfect Guards and Champion abilities

conditional.dependsOn: Second phase of the fight; dropped by a Perfect Guard, Flurry Rush, Daruk's Protection or Urbosa's Fury

campaignTags.claim: Shoots ice blocks like Waterblight Ganon
Summons fields of thunder spikes
Launches a fireball that ignites the battlefield
Swings a flaming sword

unknowns: The opened pages do not describe the Dark Beast Ganon phase or Zelda's final sealing; the end of the story is not recorded here.
His full power had he completed regeneration is unknown.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the BotW Wikipedia page (not opened) with Zelda Wiki and the Zelda Dungeon boss page. Removed "destroyed Hyrule in a single night" and "regenerative Malice layer" (not on the pages). Restored his elemental attacks, lasers and shield. Tags: broad `magic` removed (no spells named); broad `fire`, `ice` and `electric` narrowed to `fire-control`, `fire-weapon`, `ice-control` and `electric-control`.

characters.continuity: F-Zero series background (F-Zero X, F-Zero GX) with his Super Smash Bros. series moveset
characters.summary: Captain Falcon is an F-Zero champion pilot and bounty hunter with an "astronomic" record. In Smash he is a fast, heavy close-range brawler with the Falcon Punch and a fiery Falcon Kick, but no projectile.

techniques: Falcon Punch: a slow but powerful charge-up punch
Falcon Kick: a fiery flying kick
Falcon Dive: an aerial grab that ends in an explosion
Raptor Boost: a rising uppercut ("explosive" per a Melee trophy)
Final Smash (Brawl): calls the Blue Falcon and rams opponents

mechanisms: Heavy, which makes him harder to KO in Smash

weaknesses: Lacks any projectile, so opponents who keep him at range avoid his strengths (SSB)
Bad recovery (SSB)
mobility: Fastest running speed in Melee; fastest dash in SSB
Pilots the Blue Falcon, which can exceed the speed of sound

sources.supports: F-Zero background: bounty hunter with an astronomic record, pilot of the Blue Falcon, F-Zero GX Grand Prix champion, race wins over Deathborn and the Creator, Black Shadow binding him and bombing the Blue Falcon
Smash moveset (Falcon Punch, fiery Falcon Kick, Falcon Dive, Raptor Boost, Blue Falcon Final Smash), speed, weight, lack of projectile, bad recovery, Blue Falcon exceeding the speed of sound

feats.claim: Sitting champion who won the F-Zero GX Grand Prix, and beat Deathborn and the Creator in one-on-one races
Escaped after Black Shadow bound him and strapped a bomb to the Blue Falcon, by driving under a crane to knock the bomb off

conditional.ability: Blue Falcon (supersonic machine; Final Smash ram)

campaignTags.claim: Pilots the Blue Falcon F-Zero machine
Falcon Kick is a fiery flying kick

unknowns: The opened pages do not describe the Falcon Punch as fiery; only the Falcon Kick is. Combat results against named opponents are not documented (his F-Zero contests are races).
He carries a sidearm, shown used only once in the 1990 manual comic.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): replaced the cited Wikipedia page (not opened) with the F-Zero Wiki and SmashWiki pages. Replaced the vague "conquered countless tracks" feat with sourced race wins, and removed the unnamed "Smash roster" result. Removed "acrobatic dodging/reflexes" (not on the pages). Tags: `pilot` kept, `fire` kept but now rests on the fiery Falcon Kick, not the Falcon Punch.

characters.summary: Chell is Aperture Science's silent, tenacious test subject. Her only tool is the Handheld Portal Device, with which she redirected rockets to dismantle GLaDOS and later sent Wheatley into space through a portal to the Moon.

techniques: Redirects hazards through linked portals (Rocket Turret fire into GLaDOS)
Momentum flinging: momentum is conserved between portals
Destroys detached personality cores (Emergency Intelligence Incinerator)

mechanisms: Aperture Science Advanced Knee Replacements on her lower legs let her survive falls from great heights
Avoids hazards such as Goo and High Energy Pellets

weaknesses: Portals need flat, stationary surfaces of the right material (white concrete or moon rock); moving, non-flat or too-small surfaces block them
mobility: Travels through her portals with conserved momentum
limitations: The Handheld Portal Device is her only tool
No other physical or combat abilities are documented

sources.supports: Silent protagonist, tenacity, Handheld Portal Device as her only tool, Advanced Knee Replacement, defeat of GLaDOS in Portal, defeat of Wheatley via the Moon portal, GLaDOS rescuing and releasing her
Which surfaces accept portals and conservation of momentum between portals

feats.claim: Redirected Rocket Turret fire through linked portals to break GLaDOS apart and destroyed her detached cores
Fired a portal onto the Moon, pulling Wheatley into space

notableResults.note: Destroyed the personality cores; the page does not explain how she survived the neurotoxin
Linked the Moon and the Central AI Chamber; GLaDOS then rescued Chell and closed the portals, leaving Wheatley in space

conditional.dependsOn: The Handheld Portal Device and suitable flat, stationary surfaces

campaignTags.claim: Creates linked portals with the Handheld Portal Device
Handheld Portal Device and Advanced Knee Replacements
